answer: Physical delay challenge registry: each identity answers random timing challenges with a distinct unclonable circuit; the registry cross-checks delay patterns. It keeps a garden of per-identity signatures and freezes any pair whose correlation crosses a set threshold. At the nadir of a copied circuit's drift, matching jitter exposes the duplicate. The attacker pays one separate unclonable circuit and calibration per live identity, a grove of devices that cannot be shared without exposing the clone.
